payload.message: Truly excellent summary and recommendation. I want to make sure that this is captured in our documentation because I think these are the key value decisions that we're making along the way to enrich the capability of the second brain system. Truly excellent recommendation. Your one remaining choice, I agree with Your recommendation. I want this to become the standard for all of our agentic AI coding assistant integration. That includes the existing Kiro CLI, Amazon Quick, and any other integration. This will be the standard way that we integrate AI agents. We want to include their prompt and their outcome. Put those into segments, and then from there we will use the dream cycle to create more durable memories. Would you agree?

content.text:
I agree. This should be the standard ingestion model for every agentic coding assistant, not a Codex-specific feature:

`Agent Task → prompt/outcome Agent Turns → Topic Segments → Task Distillation → Dream Cycle synthesis → Express`

The documentation now records that:

- Every integration preserves the user’s prompt and visible agent outcome.
- Hidden reasoning, system instructions, tools, delegated activity, and progress commentary are excluded.
- Complete turns are grouped semantically, not by character count.
- Every qualifying Topic Segment remains stored and searchable—even if it produces no immediate memory.
- Task Distillation creates task-level decisions and insights.
- The Dream Cycle creates evaluator-gated, higher-order synthesis across memories.
- Resumed tasks refresh the same Captured Task while preserving stable completed segments.

This is captured in:

- [ADR 0002 — Agent task capture standard](</Users/kerrclaw/repositories/Github Repos/Second-Brain-work/docs/adr/0002-standardize-agent-task-capture.md>)
- [Domain glossary](</Users/kerrclaw/repositories/Github Repos/Second-Brain-work/CONTEXT.md>)
- [Capture component architecture](</Users/kerrclaw/repositories/Github Repos/Second-Brain-work/docs/CAPTURE-COMPONENTS.md:64>)
- [System architecture](</Users/kerrclaw/repositories/Github Repos/Second-Brain-work/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:62>)
- [User-guide glossary](</Users/kerrclaw/repositories/Github Repos/Second-Brain-work/docs/user-guide/glossary.md:10>)

I documented “Amazon Quick” as **Kiro CLI/Amazon Q**, matching the repository’s existing terminology.

Next decision: should we incrementally reprocess the existing Kiro and other agent histories into this new segmented model, or apply it only to new captures? I recommend an incremental historical backfill while preserving existing records until the replacement output is validated.

payload.message: One thing I caught above: Amazon Quick is a different agent framework than Kiro, and Amazon Q developer is also a different agent framework. You understand that, right, or is that not clear in the documentation?

content.text:
Yes—I understand now, and the documentation was not clear. I had incorrectly conflated them, and several older repository statements also described Kiro as routing through Amazon Q.

They are three separate products and therefore three separate integration sources:

- **Kiro** — an agentic coding service with IDE, CLI, and web surfaces. [Official Kiro documentation](https://aws.amazon.com/documentation-overview/kiro/)
- **Amazon Q Developer** — a separate developer assistant with IDE and CLI agentic coding capabilities. [Amazon Q Developer documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazonq/latest/qdeveloper-ug/what-is.html)
- **Amazon Quick** — a separate work assistant and agent platform for research, business insights, applications, and automation. [Amazon Quick documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/what-is.html)

Each requires its own Source Connector, source identity, eligibility rules, and refresh behavior. They share only the downstream standard:

`Agent Task → prompt/outcome Agent Turns → Topic Segments → Task Distillation → Dream Cycle`

I corrected the distinction in [CONTEXT.md](</Users/kerrclaw/repositories/Github Repos/Second-Brain-work/CONTEXT.md>), the [capture architecture](</Users/kerrclaw/repositories/Github Repos/Second-Brain-work/docs/CAPTURE-COMPONENTS.md:64>), the [user glossary](</Users/kerrclaw/repositories/Github Repos/Second-Brain-work/docs/user-guide/glossary.md:10>), and the older backend/operations documentation that equated Kiro with Amazon Q. The consistency check passes.

One remaining terminology question: is the repository’s existing **Quick Desktop** integration the desktop data source for **Amazon Quick**, or should Quick Desktop and Amazon Quick be treated as separate integrations?
